summary: Regorafenib is an oral multikinase inhibitor with antiangiogenic activity used for metastatic colorectal cancer, advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) after imatinib and sunitinib, and hepatocellular carcinoma after sorafenib. The recommended dose is 160 mg orally once daily for the first 21 days of each 28-day cycle, taken after a low-fat meal. It carries a BOXED WARNING for severe and sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity - monitor liver function before and during treatment and interrupt, reduce, or discontinue based on severity. Other important risks include hemorrhage, gastrointestinal perforation/fistula, severe hand-foot skin reaction and other dermatologic toxicity, hypertension, cardiac ischemia/infarction, reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome, and impaired wound healing. It is a CYP3A4 substrate - avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors.
indications: Metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF therapy, and (if RAS wild-type) an anti-EGFR therapy
Locally advanced, unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) previously treated with imatinib mesylate and sunitinib malate
Hepatocellular carcinoma previously treated with sorafenib

dosage.c: Metastatic colorectal cancer / GIST / hepatocellular carcinoma
dosage.d: 160 mg (four 40 mg tablets) orally once daily for the first 21 days of each 28-day cycle
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

dosage.d: Reduce in 40 mg increments; lowest recommended dose is 80 mg daily
dosage.n: Interrupt for Grade 2 recurrent hand-foot skin reaction and other toxicities per labeling

admin: Take 160 mg (four 40 mg tablets) at the same time each day
Swallow tablets whole with water after a low-fat meal containing less than 600 calories and less than 30% fat
Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose
Withhold for at least 2 weeks before elective surgery and do not resume until at least 2 weeks after major surgery with adequate wound healing
Monitor liver function tests before and during therapy
moa: Regorafenib is a small-molecule inhibitor of multiple membrane-bound and intracellular kinases involved in tumor angiogenesis, oncogenesis, metastasis, and tumor immunity. Regorafenib and its active metabolites M-2 and M-5 inhibit kinases including VEGFR1/2/3, TIE2, KIT, RET, RAF-1, BRAF (including BRAF V600E), PDGFR, FGFR1/2, and others, producing antiangiogenic and antitumor effects.

absolute: No contraindications are listed in the prescribing information
relative: Pre-existing hepatic impairment, especially severe (Child-Pugh C - not recommended)
High bleeding risk or active hemorrhage
Recent or planned major surgery / non-healing wounds
Uncontrolled hypertension or significant cardiac ischemic disease
monitor: Bleeding, GI perforation/fistula, cardiac ischemia, and wound healing

preg: Based on animal studies and its mechanism of action, regorafenib can cause fetal harm. It was embryolethal and teratogenic in rats and rabbits at exposures lower than the human therapeutic dose, with cardiovascular, genitourinary, and skeletal malformations. There are no human data. Advise women of reproductive potential of the risk and to use effective contraception during and for a period after treatment.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment with regorafenib and for a period (e.g., 2 weeks) after the final dose, per labeling.
renal: No clinically meaningful difference in regorafenib exposure was observed in mild to moderate renal impairment, and no dose adjustment is recommended; severe renal impairment and dialysis have not been adequately studied.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for mild (Child-Pugh A) to moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment, but these patients should be monitored closely. Regorafenib is NOT recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) as it has not been studied. Severe and fatal hepatotoxicity can occur - monitor LFTs and interrupt/reduce/discontinue per the boxed warning.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John's wort) - avoid (decrease regorafenib, reduce efficacy)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin) - avoid (increase regorafenib, increase toxicity)
moderate: BCRP substrates (e.g., methotrexate, rosuvastatin) - regorafenib may increase their exposure; monitor
Other drugs affecting hemostasis (anticoagulants/antiplatelets) - additive bleeding risk
minor: Other concomitant hepatotoxic agents (additive liver injury risk)
interactions.food: Take after a low-fat meal; a high-fat meal increases regorafenib AUC ~48% and alters metabolite levels, so a standardized low-fat meal is recommended.
interactions.alcohol: No specific alcohol interaction is described, but avoid added hepatic insult given the hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Obtain baseline and periodic liver function tests; monitor blood pressure.

common: Dysphonia, hyperbilirubinemia, fever, mucositis, weight loss, rash, nausea
serious: Severe and sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity (boxed warning)
emergency: Severe or life-threatening hemorrhage or GI perforation
RPLS (seizures, severe headache, vision loss, altered mental status)

monitoring: Liver function tests before therapy, at least every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, then periodically (boxed warning)
Blood pressure during the first cycle and as needed
Hand-foot skin reaction and other dermatologic toxicity
Signs of bleeding, GI perforation/fistula, and cardiac ischemia
counsel: Take four tablets once daily at the same time, after a low-fat meal, for 21 days then a 7-day break each cycle
Do not double up if you miss a dose
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, or right-upper-abdomen pain (liver problems) right away
Report painful red/blistering hands or feet, severe rash, chest pain, bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or very high blood pressure
Use effective contraception; do not breastfeed; tell your team before any surgery
pk: Antiangiogenic/antitumor activity via multikinase inhibition over the dosing cycle
Geometric mean Cmax ~2.5 mcg/mL at median 4 hours after a single 160 mg dose
Approximately 28 hours for regorafenib (active metabolites M-2 and M-5 have longer half-lives, ~25 and ~51 hours)
Once-daily dosing for 21 of 28 days per cycle
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); keep in original bottle with desiccant, tightly closed; discard 28 days after opening
pearls: BOXED WARNING: severe and sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity - monitor LFTs before and during treatment and interrupt/reduce/discontinue per severity
Dose is 160 mg once daily for 21 of every 28 days, taken after a low-fat meal
CYP3A4 substrate - avoid strong CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors
Class antiangiogenic risks: hemorrhage, GI perforation/fistula, hypertension, cardiac ischemia, RPLS, impaired wound healing
Hand-foot skin reaction is common and dose-limiting; hold before/after surgery
missed: If a dose is missed, take it on the same day as soon as remembered; do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose. Resume the normal once-daily schedule the next day.
overdose: The highest dose studied clinically is 220 mg per day, associated with more frequent dermatologic events, dysphonia, diarrhea, mucositis, dry mouth, decreased appetite, hypertension, and fatigue. There is no known antidote. In suspected overdose, interrupt regorafenib, institute supportive care, and observe until clinical stabilization.
